Entities, Components, And Transforms

Managed scripts access scene state through stable value handles. An Entity identifies an object within one runtime world; component and subsystem handles pair that identity with validated operations.

Entity Validity

Section titled “Entity Validity”

Entity contains a world identity and an EntityId:

Choose the validity check that matches the question:

  • entity.Id.IsValid checks whether an identity was assigned.
  • entity.IsValid also asks the active runtime whether that entity still exists.

Use Id.IsValid for cheap serialized-reference presence checks when the lifetime is already controlled. Use IsValid before operating on a reference that may have been destroyed or may belong to an expired runtime scene. default(Entity) is the invalid sentinel.

Handles do not own entities. Copying one does not keep the target alive.

Names And Active State

Section titled “Names And Active State”

Active is the object’s local setting. ActiveInHierarchy is read-only and also reflects inactive parents.

Layer is a readable/writable unsigned index from 0 through 31. It is the same value shown in the Inspector entity header and drives the owning entity’s physics collision layer. Invalid values throw before native scene state changes:

Parent And Children

Section titled “Parent And Children”

Assigning Parent preserves the world transform. SetParent lets the caller choose. The children collection is a runtime snapshot; do not assume it updates after later hierarchy changes.

Search by name or path:

Find supports /-separated segments plus . and ... A missing result is default, so check validity. Name search is ordinal and case-sensitive.

For important gameplay relationships, prefer serialized Entity fields over repeated name lookup. Names are authoring labels, not durable IDs.

Transforms

Section titled “Transforms”

Entity.Transform returns a TransformHandle:

Available properties:

Property Access Space
LocalPosition Read/write Parent-local
LocalRotation Read/write Parent-local
LocalScale Read/write Parent-local
Position Read/write World
Rotation Read/write World
Forward, Right, Up Read Derived from world rotation

Translate and Rotate accept an optional worldSpace flag. World setters preserve the authored parent relation by converting the requested value through the parent’s inverse world transform.

Adding And Removing Components

Section titled “Adding And Removing Components”

AddComponent returns an invalid handle when the operation is rejected. RemoveComponent and ComponentHandle.Remove return whether removal succeeded. Do not remove a component while another part of the current callback assumes it exists.

RequireComponent declares a permanent type-level dependency. Adding the dependent component adds missing dependencies first; removing a dependency is rejected while any attached component requires it. Duplicate, self-referential, unresolved, and cyclic dependency graphs fail managed registration without replacing the last-good registry.

Cloning And Destruction

Section titled “Cloning And Destruction”

Clone an existing scene entity:

Request destruction:

Destruction is deferred by the runtime. After requesting it, stop using the entity in gameplay logic even if a subsequent validity check in the same callback has not observed teardown yet.

Prefab assets use the separate Prefab.Instantiate API described in Gameplay Services.

Built-In Component Markers

Section titled “Built-In Component Markers”

Managed marker types support presence, enabled-state, add, and remove operations without exposing native component layout. They include:

  • transform, camera, mesh renderer, and animator;
  • collider, rigid body, and character controller;
  • audio source and listener;
  • VFX emitter;
  • directional, point, and spot lights;
  • canvas, rectangle transform, UI text, UI image, UI button, and UI layout.

These markers are deliberately empty. System-specific state uses façades such as Entity.Animator, Entity.AudioSource, RuntimeUi, and Vfx.

Entity.CharacterController is the typed movement façade. It queues collision-resolved displacement and reads the last grounded, ground-normal, and velocity state without exposing native physics ownership.

Safe Reference Pattern

Section titled “Safe Reference Pattern”

Copy the value locally when a method performs several operations. This makes it clear that all checks and mutations refer to the same serialized handle.
